title: Generation of human-induced pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cortical neurons for high-throughput imaging of neurite morphology and neuron maturation
protocol: Pre-warm cortical base media in a 37°C water bath.
Remove a frozen vial of neural progenitors from storage.
Thaw cells in a 37°C water bath by gently swirling for 1–2 minutes.
Transfer the thawed cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Dilute the 1 mL thawed cell suspension with 7 mL pre-warmed cortical base media supplemented with Y27632 (10 μM).
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Gently remove the supernatant using a vacuum suction.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of cortical base media supplemented with Y27632 (10 μM).
Perform cell counting using 10 μL of cell suspension using an automated cell counter or a hemocytometer.
Calculate the cell number and prepare the cell suspension at a density of 100,000 cells/mL media.
Seed 100 μL resuspended cell solution with a density of 100,000 cells/mL media into one well of a 96-well plate.
Confirm cells have survived, attached to the plate, and are evenly distributed within the well using a light microscope at 24 h after cell seeding.
Remove cortical base media containing Y27632 on Day 1.
Wash each well once with PBS −/− to remove residual Y27632.
Replace media with cortical differentiation base media without Y27632.
On Days 1 and 3, perform a 100% media change by replacing all 100 μL of media.
From Day 3 to Day 15, replace media with cortical maturation media supplemented with growth factors BGDAL and ϒ-secretase complex/notch pathway inhibitor (DAPT).
Add the growth factors on the day of media change to minimize degradation.
Perform media changes every second day from Days 3 to 15.
From Days 5 to 15, perform a 90% media change by removing 90 μL and adding 90 μL fresh media.
At the end of step 11, cortical neurons reach day 40 of maturation.
Aspirate media and wash wells once with PBS−/− to remove residual media.
Add 100 μL of Cytofix solution for 25 min at room temperature (20–25).
Aspirate Cytofix solution and wash cells twice with PBS−/−.
To permeabilize and block the cells for immunostaining, add Cytoperm solution for 30 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Prepare 1:1000 diluted primary antibodies in Cytoperm solution.
Aspirate the Cytoperm solution from the wells and add the diluted primary antibodies into wells.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 h.
Wash the cells twice in Cytoperm solution to remove primary antibodies.
Prepare 1:500 diluted secondary antibodies in Cytoperm solution.
Add the diluted secondary antibodies into wells.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 min.
Wash the cells twice in Cytoperm solution to remove secondary antibodies.
Prepare 1:10,000 diluted Hoechst in Cytoperm solution.
Add the diluted Hoechst into wells.
Incubate the plate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 10 min.
Wash the cells twice in Cytoperm solution to remove residual dyes.
Add 100 μL of Cytoperm solution into each well of a 96-well plate.
Seal the plates with Parafilm if samples are not imaged immediately and store at 4°C, protected from light using aluminum foil.
Image the cells within 48 hours before fluorochromes start fading.
Use Perkin Elmer PhenixPlus high content screening microscope for imaging.
Capture images under a 2× digital binning with a 16-bit Andor Zyla 5.5 megapixel sCMOS camera and a 20× water objective, resulting in an image size of 2160 × 2160 pixels.
Take z-stacked images to capture neurons at different depths.
Perform image analysis on maximum projection images.
Ensure appropriate number of image stacks are captured to image the entire depth of neurons across the well.
Acquire at least fifteen fields of view per well.
Perform image analysis using Harmony software.
Conduct neurite morphology assessment.
Measure parameters of neurite outgrowth.
Measure neurite length.
Count roots, extremities, and segments in early neurons (Day 1 post seeding neural progenitor cells).
Count roots, extremities, and segments in mature neurons (Day 15 post seeding neural progenitor cells).
Label neurons with Hoechst to identify nuclei.
Label neurons with MAP2 to identify neurites.
Image the labeled neurons.
Analyze images of neurons using an image analysis pipeline.
Segment nuclei and neurites.
Measure neurite outgrowth parameters.
Optimally segment fluorescently labelled nuclei.
Test all available pre-defined methods in the “Find nuclei” building block.
Choose the most visually convincing method for accurately selecting nuclei.
Ensure the selected method works well across different fields of view and conditions.
Conduct neuronal maturation assessment for mature neurons.
Label neurons with Hoechst to identify nuclei.
Label neurons with TBR1 or CTIP2 to identify mature cortical neurons.
Analyze images using the image analysis pipeline presented in Figure 3G (for TBR1) and 3H (for CTIP2).
Use the “find nuclei” building block to segment the image and find nuclei.
Determine fluorescence intensity of TBR1/CTIP2 markers in the nucleus region.
Set an intensity threshold using an isotype control to identify positively stained nuclei.
Measure the percentage of TBR1 and CTIP2 positive cells using the formula:
(number of TBR1/CTIP2 positive nuclei ÷ total number of Hoechst labelled nuclei) ∗ 100
Note: Measure the percentage of other mature cortical markers such as BRN2, SATB2, and CUX1 using the same image analysis pipeline.
